note: Learner-facing product framing. Goals drive onboarding and the personalised roadmap; milestones are capability claims that can only be earned through the existing deterministic evidence model. Neither file changes any evidence rule: a goal never awards evidence, and a milestone is only shown as earned when every required competency is already demonstrated in the learner's own state.

goals.title: Moving out
goals.promise: Be ready for your first weeks somewhere you run yourself.
goals.situation: You are moving out in six weeks. You need a place you can actually afford, the paperwork that comes with it, and a plan for the weeks when something goes wrong.
goals.why_useful: Most moving-out problems are not about the move. They are about a contract you did not read, a cost you did not count, or a first night with no food in the house.
sequence: Know your real monthly number before you look at any flat
Compare two homes on full cost, not the headline rent
Know what you must do in week one and what you must find out
Run the whole thing as a changing situation, not a checklist

options.label: I have somewhere and need the essentials right

options.label: Some help from family or friends

goals.title: Starting my first job
goals.promise: Handle a job, a payslip and the paperwork that comes with it.
goals.situation: You have received a first job offer. You need to check it properly, understand what you are paid and what is deducted, and keep the records that prove what happened.
goals.why_useful: A first job is where people most often agree to something they did not read. The payslip is where errors are easiest to catch and hardest to correct later.
sequence: Read an offer as a set of facts, not a compliment
Reconcile a payslip line by line and query what does not add up
Keep evidence of work done and pay received
Ask about a problem early, in writing

options.label: I have an offer to check
I have started and need to keep on top

goals.title: Starting university or college
goals.promise: Build a study routine that survives a busy week.
goals.situation: You are starting university or college. You have more to learn than time to learn it, a budget that does not stretch, and a lot of new systems to understand.
goals.why_useful: The students who struggle are rarely the ones who try hardest. They are the ones who never decided what to drop when everything became due at once.
sequence: Plan a week that survives contact with reality
Revise by testing yourself, not re-reading
Know your budget for the whole academic year, not the week
Decide what to drop when deadlines collide

options.label: Too much to do, not enough time
I study but it does not stick
Part time, alongside work or care

goals.title: Becoming more financially independent
goals.promise: Know exactly where your money goes, and what to change.
goals.situation: You want to stop being surprised by your own bank balance. An unexpected cost arrives and you need a plan before it becomes a crisis.
goals.why_useful: Financial independence is not about wealth. It is about knowing your real numbers well enough that an unexpected £300 is an inconvenience rather than an emergency.
sequence: Build a budget from your actual numbers, not a template
Survive an unexpected cost without borrowing
Understand what credit is actually costing you
Keep records that let you check anything later

questions.prompt: What is the hardest part of money right now?

options.label: I do not know where the money goes
Debt or credit I am worried about
I want to save but never do

questions.prompt: Do you keep records of anything?

goals.title: Improving general independence
goals.promise: Run the everyday things that used to need someone else.
goals.situation: You are becoming more independent: your own meals, your own home, your own appointments, your own documents, your own decisions.
goals.why_useful: Independence is not doing everything yourself. It is knowing what to do, knowing when to check, and knowing who to ask when it matters.
sequence: Keep a home working day to day
Get to the right service and be understood
Find, protect and update your own documents
Know what to do in the first ten minutes of a problem

questions.prompt: Which area is hardest right now?

options.label: Knowing what to do in a problem

goals.title: Becoming safer online
goals.promise: Tell a real request from a fake one, and act before it costs you.
goals.situation: You receive a suspicious payment request. You need to check it without falling for it, without losing access to your accounts, and without losing money you cannot replace.
goals.why_useful: Almost every online harm works the same way: create urgency, ask you to act privately, and give you a reason not to check with anyone else.
sequence: Verify an unusual request through a route the requester did not give you
Protect the account that protects everything else
Keep your backup access somewhere safe
Recognise pressure and isolation as the actual warning sign

questions.prompt: What has happened, or worries you most?

options.label: I am worried about account access
Nothing specific — I want to be safer

milestones.title: Can manage a monthly budget
milestones.description: Built a working monthly budget from real figures and kept essential costs covered when something changed.

milestones.title: Can absorb an unexpected cost
milestones.description: Responded to an unplanned expense without turning it into unmanageable debt.

milestones.title: Can reconcile a payslip
milestones.description: Checked that the pay, deductions and net amount on a payslip actually add up, and knew what to query.

milestones.title: Understands what credit really costs
milestones.description: Compared the true cost of borrowing across options rather than the headline figure.

milestones.title: Can verify a suspicious request
milestones.description: Checked an unusual request through an independent route before acting, and recognised pressure tactics.

milestones.title: Can secure the account that protects everything
milestones.description: Hardened and protected the primary account, and kept a working backup route.

milestones.title: Can compare two housing options
milestones.description: Compared homes on full ongoing and upfront cost, uncertainty and access, not just rent.

milestones.title: Can make a housing decision
milestones.description: Made and justified a housing decision under real constraints and time pressure.

milestones.title: Can organise important documents
milestones.description: Built a findable, protected set of essential records and knows where each one lives.

milestones.title: Can read a contract before signing
milestones.description: Identified the clauses that matter, including the ones that were missing.

milestones.title: Can make a complaint that gets answered
milestones.description: Escalated a problem in writing and kept a record of what happened next.

milestones.title: Can handle a realistic household problem
milestones.description: Dealt with an ordinary but inconvenient household issue end to end.

milestones.title: Can plan and prepare food on a budget
milestones.description: Planned, shopped for and prepared food using limited money and time.

milestones.title: Can check a job offer before accepting
milestones.description: Read an offer critically against what was actually agreed.

milestones.title: Can keep evidence of work and pay
milestones.description: Maintained records that prove hours worked and pay received.

milestones.title: Can ask for help and say no
milestones.description: Raised a problem clearly and held a boundary under pressure.

milestones.title: Can manage a disagreement
milestones.description: Worked through a conflict without it escalating or being avoided.

milestones.title: Can plan a week that survives
milestones.description: Built a realistic plan and decided what to drop when it stopped being possible.

milestones.title: Can get to the right service and be understood
milestones.description: Navigated access to a health or support service and got the need across.

milestones.title: Can respond to an emergency safely
milestones.description: Produced a safe ordered response and knew when to stop and call for help.

milestones.title: Can adapt a decision when things change
milestones.description: Revised an approach when the situation changed underneath it.

milestones.title: Observed preparing a simple meal
milestones.description: A suitable observer watched a safe, ordinary meal being prepared.

milestones.title: Observed restoring a sample backup
milestones.description: A suitable observer watched a backup being checked or restored safely.
